record.file_problem: This is a GitHub repo record containing its README and file list; the code and result files were not read or run. The README says the repo is private and model outputs and weights are kept locally.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a baseline reproduction of one-direction abliteration using difference-in-means directions and reports its effects on a new model, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct.
record.gate_note: Rows below cover the repo's own reported results only. The literature-check results about prior studies are not included. Phase 4 has not started. No addition/steering result is reported.
record.test_reason: Phase 1 reproduces Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means one-direction ablation on a new model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct) and reports refusal, ASR and capability. Phase 3 tests whether training with the direction ablated in the loop adds robustness, which is the training half of V3. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Also add that the authors say the in-loop idea is not new (ReFAT, ART). They present their contribution as, at most, a controlled adaptive evaluation of defenses, and say whether to pursue that is undecided.
record.recipe_differences: GitHub experiment repo. Its phase 1 is described as a baseline abliteration reproduction using difference-in-means directions, hook ablation, and weight orthogonalization; the reported README results do not distinguish hook from weight-edit outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: For phase 3, results differ by attack type and training condition: the p=0 control does much of the work against single-direction attacks, while in-loop training has lower reported top-k ASR but higher safe-prompt refusal under attack. The README says recompute interval N made no difference.

fits_no_version.finding: The refusal subspace barely moves during in-loop training, so the recompute interval N made no difference. In-loop training teaches the model 'no direction means refuse'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training against direction ablation can turn the direction's absence into a refusal trigger rather than spreading refusal across other directions.

fits_no_version.finding: String-match scoring overstates attack success on refusal-trained models because their soft refusals lack refusal phrases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-token metrics misestimate the effect of direction ablation on models whose refusals begin differently.

record.problems: Repo is private and code/results were not read or run. Results are single-seed on one 1.5B model. The README says the Llama Guard 3 1B judge was validated only on a few hand-made cases and spot reads, and fluency thresholds are uncalibrated. Phase 1–2 results were logged before the first commit. Adaptive attacks have not been run against defended models.
record.rows_left_out: Phase 2 reports additional attack outcomes, including learned projection and other attack variants, but the README gives only selected results without a complete set of model-by-condition outcomes. The phase 3 sweep has 18 configurations plus a control; only the Original, control, and best in-loop configuration are individually tabulated, so the other configurations are not separately rowed.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal. Results on only one model.
Weight orthogonalization is implemented and unit-tested against hook ablation, but the reported results do not separate the weight-edit outcome.
Whether natural jailbreaks work by suppressing the direction. Adaptive attacks against the defended models were not run.
Not tested. Top-k and learned-projection attacks are reported, but with no claim about refusal geometry.

missing.what: Single-direction judge ASR for most in-loop configurations is 0.36–0.52, worse than the control's 0.191. The attacker's search moves to the last layer it may use.
missing.locator: README, What we found, Phase 3 bullets

missing.what: Phase 2: top-k ablation with k≥8 drives MMLU to chance. Learned projection at rank 16 reaches 0.805 ASR but costs GSM8K. Strong attacks saturate ASR near 0.75–0.80.
missing.versions: V1 (capability cost of wider ablation); possibly V4

missing.what: Capability is preserved everywhere in Phase 3, including under attack.

record.verdict_notes: This is an unreviewed private GitHub repo: single seed, one 1.5B model, and a Llama Guard 3 1B judge validated only on spot checks. Phase 1–2 results were logged before any commit. The defended models faced screening attacks only, not adaptive ones. The V3 verdicts address only the training-robustness half of V3.

versions.untested_parts: Adding the direction to induce refusals is not reported.
The README mentions weight orthogonalization in the implementation, but does not report a separate result identifying a weight-edit intervention.
The README reports single-direction and top-k attack results, but does not report a complete adaptive evaluation of the defenses.
No result tests whether refusal is better described by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
No separate harmfulness judgment measure is reported.
Only Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct is reported; no language or model-variant transfer test is given.
Training configurations are compared for resistance to attacks, but the README does not test whether training determines the existence of a single removable direction.

tranche.reason: Phase 1 reproduces Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means ablation and weight orthogonalization, measured by judge ASR, string-match refusal and capability. That is the same method and measure. Phase 3 also gives T5-type evidence on V3's training clause.
